subject: "maximal number of DLLs reached..." error during simulations

messages.author: f715e5470f1e73b9
messages.subject: "maximal number of DLLs reached..." error during simulations
parts:
Hi All,

I am running simulations where during each loop I am fitting three separate models using a routine like this:


model <- nimbleModel(modelFile, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits)

cModel <- compileNimble(model, showCompilerOutput = F)

conf <- configureMCMC(model, monitors = keepers, thin = nt)

MCMC <- buildMCMC(conf)

cMCMC <- compileNimble(MCMC, project = cModel)

out <- runMCMC(cMCMC, niter = ni, nburnin = nb, nchains = 1)


After about the 100th (+/- 5) iteration of the simulation loop I get the following error:


Error in inDL(x, as.logical(local), as.logical(now), ...) : unable to load shared object '...P_294_modelFile_MID_294_06_05_02_26_20.dll': `maximal number of DLLs reached...


This has happened several times now. After the first time this error occurred, I started removing nimble created objects from the environment (e.g., all objects starting with "str.") after each model fit as well as clearing out files in the temporary directory but this didn't seem to solve the issue.

I read this link: https://developer.r-project.org/Blog/public/2018/03/23/maximum-number-of-dlls/index.html on the "maximal number of DLLs reached" error and it sounds related to the number of files created by nimble. However, this is my first time using nimble for structured simulations like this so I am unsure if this is the case. If this is due to the way I am calling nimble during my simulations (which, again, is three separate times during a single iteration of the loop), can you offer some suggestions for managing nimble files during my simulations?

Please let me know what other information you need to diagnose this issue.

Thanks for your time,
Brent

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: "maximal number of DLLs reached..." error during simulations
parts:
Hi Brent,

This has to do with an internal limit in R.

We have a feature to unload DLLs, but we have shared it only cautiously, and it isn't exported in the package namespace, because we don't feel we can guarantee it won't crash your R session.  It shouldn't, but these aspects of the system are hard for us to fully test and debug across operating systems and use cases.  So, it should work, but use with care:

nimble:::clearCompiled(obj)

where "obj" is an object (I think uncompiled or compiled but would have to verify) associated with a project, so typically either the model or the mcmc.  clearCompiled works at the project level, so once you've done it for one object in the project, you shouldn't need to do it for others.

-Perry
